statement: A pure-Rust, BSD-3-Clause port of stock zlib 1.3.1 deflate (zlib-bitexact-rs 0.131.1), patched only to take level and memLevel as arguments, reproduces 400 of 400 sampled REPDF Save As Flate streams byte-for-byte (the same 400 as OBS-0908), including the 5 that preflate-rs 0.7.6 could not reproduce without corrections; for every stream its set of matching memLevels equals stock C zlib's. It reproduces 0 of 400 Print to PDF streams, as does stock zlib. With 9 memLevels per stream it took 1.26-1.30x the wall time of stock C zlib.

Print: 400 streams; stock 0, Rust 0 (memLevel sets identical, all empty). Levels 1-3 (deflate_fast) and non-default strategies are not ported.

statement: For REPDF Save As files, the replay parameters can be calibrated from each file's own intact Flate streams, with no producer label: in all 50 C9 Save As files the intersection of memLevels that reproduce the intact streams is {7} (level 6, default strategy), and that calibration reproduces 819 of 819 original counterparts of the damaged streams. Every one of the 2,081 intact Save As original streams is replayable at memLevel 7. For Print to PDF, 1 of 1,348 original streams is replayable at all, calibration yields the empty set in 50 of 50 C9 files, and 0 of 625 counterparts replay.

statement: On 24 pages of 4 REPDF Save As originals rendered at 200 dpi, Tesseract with -l eng (the configuration TOOL-382 was verified with) recovers 2.5% of Arabic, 3.5% of Devanagari and 9.2% of Han characters, against 98.2% of Latin. With the page's script model from tessdata_best it recovers 93.8%, 88.9% and 96.1%. RapidOCR 3.9.2's default PP-OCRv6 pipeline is the best on Han (99.3%) but recovers 1.8% of Arabic and 3.1% of Devanagari; its PP-OCRv5 script recognisers reach 78.1% and 72.5%. Per-script references and margins are needed.

statement: Opening all 1,100 REPDF files with three pure-Rust loaders: hayro-syntax 0.8.0 alone opens C1 (100/100) and C10 Save As (50/50) with the original page count; lopdf 0.45.0 and pdfrum 0.4.0 open none. pdfrum recovers more text than lopdf on C5 Print (recall 1.0 vs 0, lopdf opens with 0 pages), C6 Save As (0.578 vs 0, but precision 0.485, i.e. plausible-but-wrong text) and C9 (Save As 0.701 vs 0.645, Print 0.614 vs 0.463). No library panicked. Text recall is against the same library's text of the matching original; hayro-syntax has no text API, so only open and page count were measured for it.

statement: REPDF's C7 and C8 files keep no embedded font program anywhere in the file, not even as unreferenced objects, and C8 also keeps no CMap stream; C6 keeps nearly all programs and ToUnicode maps. So in C8 only font names, encodings, widths and the content-stream codes survive, and glyph-shape recovery has nothing to read. Separately, leaving one Save As base document out, 93.1% of its ToUnicode entries (font name without subset tag, code) also occur in the other 49 documents' maps, and 94.0% of those agree: a mapping fitted on other base documents decodes most of a held-out document, so a split by base document alone does not hold font knowledge out.
